comment: Keystone THREADS for the year, plus the recap ITEMS the built lessons have authored. Under DFM 134 the Do-Now serves a pupil only items from lessons she has COMPLETED, so each item is authored by the lesson that teaches it and added when that lesson is built. Lesson 1 has no Do-Now of its own; its five items are served from Lesson 2 onwards. Year-One note (his K4 ruling): this cohort arrives with no platform history and no Python, so nothing here assumes a J1 or J2 thread — J3 L1 and L2 establish their own ground first.

kp-platform-j3.label: How this website works
kp-platform-j3.note: First-ever login for this cohort. Established J3 L1; deliberately not inherited from J1.

kp-code-j3.label: The studio code
kp-code-j3.note: The DT room rules taught as what professionals do, and tested by judgement in J3 L1.

kp-py-basics.label: Python from zero: print, variables, running a program
kp-py-basics.note: Established J3 L2, the Year-One lesson added because this cohort has no Python (his K4 taper).

kp-list.label: Lists: holding a set of values

kp-function.label: Functions and parameters
kp-function.note: Established L4; the reuse idea the sprint leans on.

kp-debug.label: Finding and naming a fault in code
kp-debug.note: Established L5. Sorting and searching are deliberately NOT here — decided 17 Jul, left for GCSE.

kp-data-insight.label: Turning query results into an insight
kp-data-insight.note: Established L6; picks up J2's kp-query for pupils who have it.

kp-ml-pattern.label: How a machine learns a pattern

kp-genai-verify.label: Checking what AI gives you
kp-genai-verify.note: Established L8. The verification habit, not the tool.

kp-ai-ethics.label: The costs and ethics of AI
kp-ai-ethics.note: Established L9, environmental cost included. Stat cards must be sourced before go-live.

kp-user-story.label: User-centred design and user stories
kp-user-story.note: Established L10; the sprint in L11 is judged against these.

kp-prototype.label: Building and testing a prototype
kp-prototype.note: Established L11. Year-One: a micro:bit gadget is one of the build mediums.

kp-accessibility.label: Making work usable by everybody
kp-accessibility.note: Established L12. New-engine flag: contrast gate and keyboard-only simulators need a prototype first.

kp-routes.label: The two GCSE routes and their shared core
kp-routes.note: Opened in L1's compass, tried out in L14/L15, decided in L16, reviewed in L17.

items.stem: Méabh leaves at the bell without signing out. The next pupil sits down at that machine and deletes a folder by accident. When the school checks who deleted it, which name comes up?
options: Méabh's, because the machine was still signed in as her
The next pupil's, because she is the one who did it
Nobody's, because the school cannot tell who was at a machine
The teacher's, because they are in charge of the room

items.stem: Ciara sits down and finds the machine still signed in as somebody from the last class, with their work open on the screen. What should she do?
options: Sign that person out without reading their work, then sign in as herself
Close the work down and carry on working in that person's account
Read enough of it to find out whose it is, then go and tell the teacher
Move to a different machine and say nothing about it to anybody

items.stem: Sinéad opens her year map and finds Lesson 3 has a padlock on its tile, and the class was told they are doing Lesson 3 today. What should she do?
options: Tell her teacher, because a padlock means nobody has opened it yet
Refresh the page until the padlock disappears from the tile
Start Lesson 4 instead, because that tile has no padlock
Wait, because a padlocked lesson opens by itself at lesson time

items.stem: It is June. Róisín's teacher puts the same twelve questions on the screen that she answered in her very first DT lesson back in September. Why is she doing them a second time?
options: So she can see for herself how much she has learned
So her teacher can work out the mark for her report
So the teacher can decide which class she is in next year
So the website knows which lessons to open for her

items.stem: Aoibhe comes in from break with a bottle of water and stands it beside the keyboard with the lid screwed on. Her teacher asks her to move it. Why?
options: Nothing to drink goes near the machines, lid on or lid off
Water is fine, but the bottle has to sit on the floor under the desk
Water is fine, but she needed to ask a teacher before bringing it in
Only fizzy drinks are banned near the machines, and water is not one

items.stem: Sorcha needs the console to show the words Doors open at 7 and nothing else. Which line does that?
options: It is a print line with the words inside speech marks inside the brackets
It is a print line with the words inside brackets and no speech marks
It is a line that has the words on their own and nothing round them
It is a line with an = sign and the words after it

items.stem: Aoife's program has `venue = "The Harbour Light"` near the top, and uses venue on four later lines. The show moves to a different theatre. How many lines does she change?
options: One — the line with the = on it
Four — every line that mentions venue
Five — the one with the = and the four that use it
None — the program works it out

items.topic: A sum inside a printed line
items.stem: A line reads `print("Seats left: " + str(120 - 87))`. What does the console show?
options: Seats left: 33
Seats left: 120 - 87
Seats left:

items.stem: A list holds four titles. Which one does `playlist[2]` give you?
options: It gives you the third one
It gives you the second one
It gives you the fourth one
It gives you all four, up to number 2

items.stem: A list holds four titles. What does `len(playlist)` give you, and what is the LAST position in the list?
options: 4, and the last position is 3
4, and the last position is 4
3, and the last position is 4
4, and there is no last position

items.stem: Róisín's list holds five titles. She runs `playlist.append("One More")`. How many titles does the list hold now?
options: Six — the new one goes on the end
One — the new one replaces what was there
Five — the new one is printed instead
Six — the new one goes at the front

items.stem: Ciara writes `order = playlist.sort()` and then prints order. The console shows None. What has happened?
options: sort put the list in order and handed nothing back
sort could not put the list in order
sort emptied the list
sort needs a number in the brackets

items.stem: A list holds three titles, and a loop reads `for song in playlist:` with one printing line indented under it. How many lines appear on the console?
options: Three lines appear, one for each title
One line appears, because the loop runs once
Four lines appear: three titles and one naming the list
No lines appear, because a loop does not print

items.stem: Saoirse's `playlist.remove("curtain up")` line is not taking anything out, and her list definitely holds Curtain Up. Why?
options: The capital letters do not match
remove only works on the first title in a list
remove needs a position, not a title
The list has to be sorted first

items.stem: A list holds six titles. What does `playlist[0:3]` give you?
options: It gives you the first three titles
It gives you the first four titles
It gives you the titles at positions 0 and 3 only
It gives you the whole list, starting at 0

items.stem: A show has forty songs. Why is one list better than forty separate boxes with forty names?
options: One name lets you count them, order them and go through them all at once
Forty boxes would use too much of the computer's memory
Python only allows a small number of boxes in one program
There is no difference — a list is just forty boxes with one name
